r.name: Via Alpina Blue D3
r.description: Alpe Devero - Binn

r.name: G24 - Rif. Maria Luisa - Bta di Valmaggia

r.description: Beautiful walk through larch trees until Pian du Scricc then climb up to Pian Sass Mor, a steep rampart precedes the Valtendra Pass, a long traverse up to the Scatta d'Orogna, the flat Val Buscagna and a last steep descent leads to the Devero

r.name: H99 - Alpe Devero - Passo di Valtendra
r.description: The initial stretch to go up to Val Buscagna is tiring, then it is a long, almost flat walk with a short steep stretch for the Scatta d'Orogna, steep descent to the lake and to Val Bondolero then ascent to Valtendra

r.name: H00 - Via dell'Arbola da Baceno al Devero (prima sezione)

r.description: Sentiero Italia - Tappa E62A
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E61
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E63
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E65
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E64

r.name: H00 - Via dell' Arbola dal Devero a Binn (seconda sezione, tratto italiano)
Via dell' Arbola Tappa 2 - Dal Devero a Binn (tratto svizzero)
H09 - Cravegna - Alpe Agarù. Parte della Veia di Scuettar
r.description: The Veia di Scuettar or Via degli Scoiattoli was once traveled with herds by the inhabitants of Crodo to reach Alpe Devero along a hillside route. To complete it follow H09x and then H09y, the latter very dangerous due to landslide

r.name: H07 - Goglio - Colle di Ciamporino
r.description: The path up to Cima Piaggio is very steep, then a long and shady dirt road and another steep stretch to reach the vast meadows of Alpe Bondolero and then the slopes of San Domenico ski.

r.name: F16 - San Domenico - Monte Cistella
r.description: Long but rewarding climb. From the summit of Monte Cistella the view is spectacular at 360 °. Suitable for normal hikers except for a short final stretch under the summit which requires a short climb, there is a chain (2022).

r.name: H03 - Al Passo - Bocchetta di Deccia
r.description: Initially on a road then steep and tiring with a track often overrun by grasses, final stretch on stony ground and then on an exposed path, well paint marked

r.name: G06 - Verampio - Aleccio
r.description: Steep mule track that from the footbridge on the Marmite dei Giganti leads first to Crego and then to Aleccio

r.name: G34 - Verampio - Premia
r.description: Dirt road that climbs from Verampio to Premia along the entrances to the Marmitte dei Giganti and the Gorges of the area

r.name: G27 - Le Casse - Passo del Muretto
G19 - San Rocco - Casarola di sopra
r.description: Very steep and tiring path with a thin and sometimes non-existent track in the upper part

r.name: H16 - Crampiolo - Passo del Muretto
r.description: Starting in Crampiolo, reachable from Alpe Devero, well signposted, it runs through larch woods up to Alpe Sangiatto, then on high altitude meadows, passes the B.ta di Scarpia, descends to Alpe Pojala, climbs another hill and arrives at the Muretto Pass

r.name: H08 - Goglio - Passo di Pojala
r.description: First you go up the road, then the long Enel service tunnel, then you go along Lake Agaro, go past a high bastion up to Alpe Pojala and from here high altitude meadows up to the lake of the same name and finally the Pass

r.name: H06 - Croveo - Diga di Agaro
r.description: Interesting very scenic route on the ancient mule track that went up to the Walser village of Agaro now submerged by the lake. You pass many pastures and the sunny and panoramic balcony of Piodacalva

r.name: H08c - Lago Agaro - Passo di Topera
r.description: Landscaped and panoramically interesting route, unfortunately the central part is overrun by rhododendrons and GPS is essential to keep on track

r.name: H04 - Croveo - Diga di Agaro
r.description: Path for experts has some sections with chains and often strong exposure

r.name: G21 - Passo - Salecchio Superiore
r.description: Easy and profitable route that reaches the Walser settlement of Salecchio, an unlit tunnel is easily circumvented with a marked route

r.name: H01a - Fraccio - Alpe Deccia
r.description: The route runs along the Chapels of the Misteri del Santo Rosario to the Oratory of the Madonna di Salera then the beautiful meadows of Compolo, a very steep final stretch on a barely visible trail, but the Deccia meadows repay the effort
Sentiero Italia - Tappa E62B

r.name: G31 - Lago Vannino - Bocchetta della Valle
r.description: You go along the Vannino Lake then up to the beautiful prairies at the Busin Pass, a short hillside, danger of stones, with a wonderful view of Monte Giove and Lower Busin Lake, along the upper Busin Lake and with a short ascent the B.ta della Valle

r.name: G14 - Foppiano - Alpe Cramec
r.description: Path that from Foppiano leads to Alpe Cramec and the homonymous lake, through Alpe Croce

r.name: G00 - Via del Gries da Crevoladossola a Baceno (prima sezione)
r.description: The route follows beautiful mule tracks, a stretch of dirt track after Pontemaglio and village streets within the hamlets

r.name: G00 - Via del Gries da Baceno a Ponte (seconda sezione)
r.description: The route follows beautiful mule tracks and country lanes within the hamlets. It does not present particular difficulties and is on well-marked paths

r.name: G00 - Via del Gries da Ponte a Riale (terza sezione)
r.description: Path in an alpine environment of Walser culture. Spectacular view of the Toce waterfall (which opens at times)

r.name: G00 - Via del Gries da Riale a Passo del Gries (quarta sezione)
r.description: From Riale to a little beyond Lake Morasco, proceed by road then begin the route on alpine paths passing through Bettelmat and then the steep climb that leads to Passo del Gries

r.name: G30 - Cagiogno - Aleccio
r.description: From Cagiogno, by mule track, to the beautiful Bee mountain pasture from which, by a path that is exposed at times on the hillside, you reach the Aloro mountain pasture. Following a forest road, you reach the equipped area of Piana di Aleccio

r.name: L98 - Rifugio Sironi - Passo della Fria - Confine Svizzero
L99 - Rifugio Sironi - Bocchetta del Lago Gelato
G36 - Crego - Maglioggio
r.description: Easy flat path, for a long stretch you walk on a covered canal, but which for a short slippery stretch and with chains cannot be classified as tourist

r.name: G38 - Cruppo - Crego
r.description: From Cruppo a paved mule track climbs to Dugno then the path climbs very steeply until it reaches the Aleccio road, and then continues on asphalt to Crego

r.name: G10 - San Rocco - Alpe Groppo
r.description: Very steep and tiring path with a thin and sometimes non-existent track in the upper part. Exceptional panorama at Alpe Groppo where there is a bivouac

r.name: G12 - Passo - Alpe Groppo
r.description: Very steep and tiring path with a track beyond Pianezza di sopra overgrown with vegetation and GPS needed to find it

r.name: G32 - Crego - Cagiogno
r.description: The route follows a water main for a good part.

r.name: G20 - Riale - Passo di San Giacomo
G22 - Lago Castel - Bta di Tamia
r.description: Up to Lake Nero, suitable for mountain hikers, after Lake Nero the exposure and steepness of the trail reserve it for experts. There are long stretches of stone. However, the very frequent blue trail signs make it easier to find the trail (2024)

r.name: G24a - Laghi del Boden - Passo di San Giacomo
r.description: Flat route apart from the small climb to Rupe del Gesso. The path has been adapted for bicycle transit. Very panoramic and you return to Rif. Maria Luisa along the dirt road that runs alongside Lake Toggia

r.name: G28 - Rif. Maria Luisa - Punta Valrossa
G22a - Cascata del Toce - Lago Castel
r.description: Very steep route with steps up to Alpe Ghighel then more relaxing among flowery meadows and peat bogs unfortunately a ford with steep steps can create difficulties

r.name: G18 - Canza - Bta di Tamia
r.description: Up to Alpe Tamia suitable for mountain hikers, after Alpe Tamia for the difficulty of finding the route due to the lack of track and trail signs and for the exposure on the final bare rock, it is reserved for experts

r.name: G97 - Alpe Vannino - Passo di Nefelgiù
r.description: Dirt surface path that leads from the Eugenio Margaroli Refuge and the Italo Valmaggia Bivouac to the Nefelgiù Pass

r.name: G25 - Alpi di Vova - Lago Busin Inferiore
r.description: Very steep path, initially in a dense coniferous forest, then on prairies and finally a steep and exposed hump overcomes the final bastion

r.name: G35 - Cascata del Toce - Lago Vannino
G35a - Sottofrua - Alpe Freghera di sopra
G39 - Lago Morasco - Rifugio 3A
r.description: A channel with rocky steps leads to a plateau from which a long stretch along the hillside leads to the Sabbioni lake which is skirted and with a steep climb to the Claudio and Bruno refuge. A long half-hillside with a steep final climb leads to 3A refuge

r.name: G95 - Lago di Morasco - Passo di Nefelgiù
G41 - Bettelmat - Lago dei Sabbioni
r.description: A very popular route that starts from the Bettelmatt mountain pasture, famous for its cheeses, passes through the Rif. Città di Busto divalla passing under the dam of the Lago dei Sabbioni and goes back up to the ex Mores and Somma Lombardo refuges.

r.name: G41a - Piano dei Camosci - Rifugio 3A
r.description: Route almost entirely on scree and rocks, very frequent cairns and painted signs, modified the old route that passed over the ex glacier

r.name: G43 - Sentiero Castiglioni
r.description: Very panoramic, suitable for expert hikers, some very exposed ways with some help chains, the final part follows the moraines on which the Swiss border runs

r.name: G00d - Ponte - Sotto Frua
r.description: Variant for paths to the Via del Gries G00 which mainly uses the road. Much used by MTB (signs) pay attention.

r.name: G17 - Premia - La Pioda
r.description: Initially gentle path on the meadows of Altoggio then from the Madonna dell'Oro it climbs with a long stairway up to the upper edge of precipices which it runs along until its end near a beautiful waterfall

r.name: H14 - Lago di Devero - Bocchetta della Valle
r.description: From the H98 you go up into a larch forest coming out to the Alpe della Valle, then to the Alpe Naga and at the crossroads with H08 which goes up to the Pojala Pass you head to the left and proceeding halfway up the hill you reach at the B.ta della Valle

r.name: H98 - Crampiolo - Scatta Minoia
r.description: Path on a dirt road to Alpe Forno then a path to Scatta Minoia. Possible loop with return on the beautiful plateaus rich in lakes of H12 from Alpe Forno to Alpe Sangiatto where a dirt road leads back to Crampiolo

r.name: H17 - Alpe Codelago - Passo di Crampiolo
H98a - Alpe Devero - Crampiolo
r.description: Winter route to Crampiolo which avoids the dangerous part of H98

r.name: H15 - ALpe Devero - Passo della Rossa
H11 - Alpe Devero - Monte Cazzola
r.description: The route begins in a larch forest to Alpe Misanco; beyond this point, the vegetation thins out and eventually disappears, and the path continues through an almost lunar landscape to the Buscagna Lakes and, finally, to our destination.

r.name: H10 - Alpe Devero - Diga di Agaro
r.description: Interesting route: the waterfalls of the Devero stream, vast panoramas of the mountains surrounding the Devero from Cistella to Pizzo Crampiolo, arrival in a dive on Lake Agaro

r.name: H00e - Forcola - Cologno
r.description: Short connection between the H00 and H10 routes, useful for parking without cost and reaching Alpe Devero via Forcola on H00 or via Cologno on H10

r.name: H09c - Ponte della Baulina - Veia di Scuetar
r.description: Initially easy and clearly visible path up to Foglieggio where it becomes less evident and steep and tiring up to Veia di Scuetar

r.name: H01 - Baceno - Cravegna - Deccia - Bta di Deccia
r.description: Very long and tiring journey. As there are roads, it is advisable to reach Deccia starting from Foppiano (the Deccia road has a barrier) following the G09 up to Prepiana (Voma) from where you reach the Deccia road to the right

r.name: H09a - Bivio H09 - Deccia
r.description: The route starts at the H09 Veia di Scuetar junction and climbs through a dense forest of larch and fir trees, crossing several avalanche gullies. At Alpe Deccia, there is a view over the Devero and Antigorio valleys.

r.name: H09y - Pian di Rio Secco - Bivio H0. Parte della Veia di Scuettar
r.description: Route that is part of the Veia di Scuettar, but reserved for very expert hikers. ATTENTION in front of the Rio Freddo waterfall the path is affected by a long-standing landslide still active, it is easy to pass but it is very dangerous.

r.name: H09x - Alpe Agarù - Pian di Rio Secco. Parte della Veia di Scuettar
r.description: Always on dirt road that joining the two sections H09 and H09y of the Veia di Scuettar completes it from Cravegna to the mule track that from Goglio climbs to Alpe Devero

r.name: 14a-Sentiero dei passi alpini
r.description: Cette variante n'est pas répertoriée en Suisse Mobil

r.name: H18 - Grande Est Alpe Devero
r.description: it is a walk on the plains of the Great East.Profitable route for landscapes and views from above on Alpe Devero and Codelago

r.name: 10 - Rifugio Maria Luisa - Piano delle Creste
11 Capanna Piano delle Creste - Capanna Grossalp
